title: Intracranial Pressure Monitoring Trend
scenario: A 42-year-old client with a traumatic brain injury has an intraventricular catheter for continuous intracranial pressure (ICP) monitoring. The nurse reviews the flowsheet of ICP, cerebral perfusion pressure, and neuro findings over six hours.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Reviewing the flowsheet, how should the nurse interpret the trend?

options.text: Rising ICP with falling cerebral perfusion pressure and declining GCS indicates worsening increased intracranial pressure
The trend is within normal limits and requires only routine monitoring
The falling cerebral perfusion pressure reflects improving cerebral blood flow
The changes indicate resolving cerebral edema

questions.rationale: ICP climbed from 12 to 30 mmHg (normal 5-15) while CPP fell to 52 mmHg (target above 60) and GCS dropped from 14 to 8 with a new fixed pupil, a clear pattern of worsening intracranial hypertension and impending herniation.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Based on the deteriorating trend, which nursing actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Notify the provider immediately of the rising ICP and declining GCS
Elevate the head of the bed to 30 degrees with the head midline
Ensure the airway is patent and prepare to support oxygenation
Anticipate an order for osmotic diuretic such as mannitol
Cluster nursing care and suction frequently to keep the client stimulated
Place the client flat with the neck flexed toward the chest

questions.rationale: Worsening intracranial hypertension requires urgent provider notification, head-of-bed elevation with neutral neck alignment to promote venous drainage, airway and oxygenation support, and osmotic diuretics. Clustering stimulating care and flat positioning with neck flexion raise ICP further.
